summary: The data indicates an exclusive reliance on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without carbohydrate logging, complicated by delayed gastric emptying from GLP-1 medication. This reactive dosing approach, combined with excessively high maximum insulin limits, leads to severe insulin stacking and recurrent hypoglycemia, particularly overnight and in the early evening.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithms dose insulin reactively based on rising glucose levels. Without knowing the carbohydrate amount upfront, the system can only guess meal size from the glucose spike.

GLP-1 medications slow digestion, causing carbohydrate absorption to peak much later than normal. A reactive algorithm may wait to bolus until the late spike occurs, meaning insulin action will peak even later, often long after the meal is over.

Safety limits like max IOB (Insulin on Board) and max basal are critical guardrails. Setting them too high allows the loop to aggressively chase spikes without restricting delivery to biologically safe amounts.
strengths: Excellent continuous glucose monitor connectivity with 98.7% coverage and minimal gaps.
High time in range during the early morning hours, reaching 97.5% at 05:00 and 98.7% at 06:00.
issues: Severe hypoglycemia, heavily clustered at night (18.5% time below range at 00:00, 10.1% at 01:00) and early evening (15.3% at 18:00).
Extreme and unsafe AAPS limits configured, with Max IOB at 25 U and Max Basal at 12 U/h, which is vastly disproportionate to the typical 0.5-0.8 U/h basal requirement.
Complete lack of carbohydrate logging forces the loop to manage all meals reactively, exacerbating insulin stacking due to GLP-1 delayed absorption.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The configured maximum IOB of 25 U poses an immediate severe hypoglycemia risk. These limits must be reduced drastically before altering underlying basal or target settings.

analysis_steps.findings: The highest priority is resolving the extreme max IOB and basal limits to prevent severe UAM-driven insulin stacking. Following this, raising the overnight target will provide a safety buffer against residual late evening dosing. Finally, logging carbs is required to transition away from pure reactive UAM.
analysis_steps.evidence: TBR is severe (18.5%), limits are extreme (25U IOB), zero carbs logged.

recommendations.title: Reduce maximum safety limits immediately
recommendations.description: The configured max IOB of 25 U and max basal of 12 U/h are excessively dangerous for a profile with a 0.6 U/h baseline. When relying on UAM for delayed digestion spikes, these limits allow massive, uncontrolled insulin stacking that leads directly to severe nighttime hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Raise overnight and late-evening targets
recommendations.description: The current 90 mg/dL target at 23:00 and 00:00 leaves zero margin for error when insulin from the evening is still acting. Raising this target will prompt the system to suspend basal sooner, buffering against nighttime lows.

recommendations.title: Begin logging carbohydrates
recommendations.description: Exclusive reliance on Unannounced Meals (UAM) while taking GLP-1 medication forces AAPS to react aggressively to delayed spikes. Announcing meals with carbohydrate entries allows AAPS to pace insulin delivery and reduces aggressive late-SMB stacking.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Target at 00:00 and 23:00 is too tight at 90 mg/dL given the 18.5% time below range observed. A higher target is necessary to provide the algorithm a safety buffer to suspend insulin earlier before hypoglycemia occurs.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight time below range for 3 days after raising the target and reducing the safety limits.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Increase the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 mg/dL to 110 mg/dL.

parameter_decisions.rationale: A max IOB of 25 U is approximately 150% of the estimated total daily basal, permitting massive insulin stacking by the UAM algorithm. Must be heavily restricted.
Dynamic ISF is functioning as designed, though it was improperly leveraging the unsafe max limits. Evaluate its performance only after limits are corrected.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition away from purely unannounced meals by logging carbohydrate sizes manually, to prevent reactive UAM from stacking insulin excessively behind delayed GLP-1 glucose peaks.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Because zero carbohydrates are recorded, AAPS is forced to bolus reactively to spikes. GLP-1 usage delays digestion, meaning the glucose spike arrives late, causing AAPS to deliver massive insulin too late and pushing glucose into severe nighttime hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log all carbohydrate intake for 5 to 7 consecutive days to reveal true insulin-to-carb responses and absorption duration.

implementation_steps: 1. Reduce AAPS safety limits immediately (`max_iob_units` to 5 U and `max_basal_u_per_hour` to 3 U/h) to prevent the algorithm from delivering massive, unrecoverable reactive doses.
2. Raise the overnight profile targets at 23:00 and 00:00 to 110 mg/dL to provide a wider safety margin against late-evening insulin stacking.
3. Begin logging approximate carbohydrate amounts for meals, allowing the system to anticipate insulin needs rather than waiting for delayed glucose spikes.
